guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: [Lyons et al., Back, Teebken et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Once vascular graft/endograft infection is suspected, exhaustive evaluation of clinical status, signs of infection and patient comorbidities according to the MAGIC criteria is recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Baron et al.
rec_text_verbatim: When a vascular graft/endograft infection is suspected, it is recommended that every effort is made to obtain microbiological proof of infection.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Baron et al., Padberg et al.
rec_text_verbatim: To obtain microbiological proof of vascular graft/endograft infection, the yield of at least three deep rather than superficial samples should be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Scherrer et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Microbiological investigation of negative pressure wound therapy foams should not be performed in order to support the diagnosis of vascular graft/endograft infection.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Wengrowitz et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Sonification of intra-operatively harvested graft material may be considered in order to improve the micro-organism detection rate.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Bruggink et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients suspected of vascular graft/endograft infection, the use of ultrasound as the sole diagnostic modality is not recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Reinders Folmer et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For suspected vascular graft/endograft infection, CTA is recommended as the first line diagnostic modality.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Shahidi et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients suspected of vascular graft/endograft infection, if CTA is contra-indicated, the use of MRA may be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Reinders Folmer et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a clinical suspicion of vascular graft/endograft infection and with non-convincing findings on CTA, the use of 18F-FDG-PET combined with low dose CT is recommended as an additional imaging modality to improve diagnostic accuracy.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Reinders Folmer et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In patients with a clinical suspicion of peripheral vascular graft/endograft infection, single photon emission computed tomography, if available, is recommended as an additional imaging modality to improve diagnostic accuracy.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Stewart et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In every case where a vascular graft/endograft is implanted, antimicrobial prophylaxis to cover the first 24 hours, by intravenous administration of a first/second generation cephalosporin or vancomycin in the event of penicillin allergy, is recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Habib et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Before implantation of any vascular graft/endograft, elimination of any potential source of sepsis, especially of dental origin, should be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Habib et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Antimicrobial prophylaxis to prevent vascular graft/endograft infection should be considered before any dental procedure involving the manipulation of the gingival or peri-apical region of teeth or perforation of the oral mucosa, including scaling and root canal procedures for patients previously operated on with a vascular/endovascular graft.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Darouiche, Revest et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Antimicrobial therapy is recommended in every patient with an infected graft/endograft.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Consensus of expert opinion
rec_text_verbatim: For the diagnosis and treatment of vascular graft/endograft infection it is recommended that the patient be transferred to specialised high volume centre with multidisciplinary experience in this pathology.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Lazaris et al.
rec_text_verbatim: When patch corrugation is found on ultrasound follow up after carotid endarterectomy further investigations may be considered to exclude a vascular graft infection.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Lejay et al., Son et al., Grazziotin et al., Kaviani et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with supra-aortic trunk vascular graft/endograft infection, total removal of infected material followed by reconstruction with autologous material is recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Kragsterman et al., Thorbjornsen et al.
rec_text_verbatim: The EndoVAC technique may be considered as a treatment option in selected patients with supra-aortic trunk vascular graft/endograft infection when neither total removal of infected material nor when usual conservative VAC therapy are considered feasible or safe.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Younis et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In the emergency setting with active bleeding in patients with supra-aortic trunk vascular graft/endograft infection, a combined endovascular and surgical approach may be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Myles et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Conservative treatment, including antimicrobial therapy without reconstruction, for supra-aortic trunk vascular graft/endograft infection may be considered for patients unfit for surgery.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Lyons et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For persistent fever or inflammatory symptoms after implantation of a thoracic graft/endograft, further diagnostic investigations are recommended in the search for infection.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Kahlberg et al., Moulakakis et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For fit patients with proven thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, total graft explantation is recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Spiliotopoulos et al., Roselli et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with *in situ* reconstructions of thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, coverage of the newly inserted graft with autologous, and ideally vascularised, tissue is recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Czerny et al., Kahlberg et al., Chiesa et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with thoracic vascular graft/endograft infection that are at major risk of surgery, conservative treatment may be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Kahlberg et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with suspected thoracic graft/endograft infection, in the absence of fistulisation to the oesophagus or airway, or generalised sepsis, prolonged antimicrobial therapy combined with drainage of peri-graft fluid and/or irrigation, may be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Kahlberg et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, partial explantation may be considered if infection is limited.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Smeds et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For the reconstruction of thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, cryopreserved allografts may be considered the first choice graft material.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Roselli et al.
rec_text_verbatim: After extra-anatomic reconstruction for thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, reinforcement of the aortic stump with autologous, and ideally vascularised, tissues should be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Kahlberg et al., Moulakakis et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with aorto-oesophageal fistula complicating thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, explantation of the infected material, repair of the oesophagus, and coverage with viable tissue is recommended as definitive treatment.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Chiesa et al., Chiesa et al., Canaud et al., Canaud et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In the emergency setting with active bleeding complicating thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection with an aorto-oesophageal fistula, initial treatment with an aortic endograft, as a bridge to definitive treatment, should be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Czerny et al., Chiesa et al., Smeds et al., Chiesa et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Conservative treatment of patients with an aorto-oesophageal fistula complicating thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection is not recommended, except in a palliative setting.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Czerny et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Treatment of aorto-oesophageal fistula complicating thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection with an oesophageal endoprosthesis alone is not recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Czerny et al., Chiesa et al., Chiesa et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In patients with aortobronchial or aortopulmonary fistula complicating thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, closure of the airway defect and explantation of the infected material with *in situ* reconstruction should be considered as definitive treatment.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Canaud et al., Canaud et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In the emergency setting of active bleeding complicating thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection with an aortobronchial or aortopulmonary fistula, treatment with an aortic endograft should be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Canaud et al., Canaud et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with an aortobronchial or aortopulmonary fistula complicating thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, preservation of the endograft may be considered after closure of the airway defect and coverage with viable tissue.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Kahlberg et al., Spiliotopoulos et al., Kahlberg et al., Luehr et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For all patients treated for thoracic/thoraco-abdominal vascular graft/endograft infection, lifelong follow up is recommended because of the risk of recurrent infections or fistulae.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Calligaro et al., Batt et al., Ohta et al., Igari et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Percutaneous drainage of peri-graft fluid with or without irrigation may be considered for microbiological identification and to reduce the bacteriological burden, but not as ultimate treatment in abdominal aortic graft/endograft infection.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Batt et al., O'Connor et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For fit patients with an abdominal aortic vascular graft/endograft infection, complete excision of all graft material and infected tissue is recommended for definitive treatment.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Batt et al., Spiliotopoulos et al., Dorigo et al., Dorweiler et al., Heinola et al., Ali et al., Harlander-Locke et al., O'Connor et al., Rodrigues dos Santos et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with an abdominal aortic vascular graft/endograft infection, <i>in situ reconstruction with autologous vein should be considered as the preferred method.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Batt et al., Spiliotopoulos et al., Dorigo et al., Dorweiler et al., Heinola et al., Ali et al., Harlander-Locke et al., O'Connor et al., Rodrigues dos Santos et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with abdominal aortic vascular graft/endograft infection, cryopreserved allografts, silver coated grafts, rifampicin bonded polyester grafts, or bovine pericardium should be considered as alternative solutions.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Mirzaie et al., Simmons et al., Phang et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Partial excision of infected an aortic vascular graft/endograft may be considered when infection is documented as limited and the remaining material is well incorporated.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Oderich et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with abdominal aortic vascular graft/endograft infection and a large abscess or multiresistant micro-organisms, extra-anatomic reconstruction may be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Lejay et al., Harlander-Locke et al., Touma et al., Kieffer et al.,
rec_text_verbatim: Lifelong imaging follow up is recommended after *in situ* reconstruction with cryopreserved allografts for abdominal aortic vascular graft/endograft infection, in order to detect allograft degeneration.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Miyamoto et al., Schoell et al.
rec_text_verbatim: Securing a supracoeliac clamp zone or using an aortic occlusion balloon may be considered as the first step before entering the aorto-enteric fistula area.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Chick et al., Batt et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In the emergency setting of active bleeding complicating abdominal aortic graft/endograft infection with or without aorto-enteric fistula, initial treatment with an endograft should be considered, but only as a temporary measure.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Rodrigues dos Santos et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In surgical repair of aortic abdominal graft/endograft infection with aorto-enteric fistula, omentoplasty or transfer of autologous vascularised tissue to cover the vascular reconstruction is recommended.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: van den Bergh et al., Das et al., Malgor et al., Madoff et al., Pillai et al.
rec_text_verbatim: In the emergency setting of active bleeding complicating abdominal aortic graft/endograft infection with an arterio-ureteral fistula, initial treatment with an endograft may be considered, but only as a temporary measure.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: van den Bergh et al., Das et al., Malgor et al., Madoff et al., Pillai et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with an arterio-ureteral fistula and vascular graft/endograft infection, complete explantation of the graft combined with urological treatment with or without *in situ* arterial reconstruction should be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Siracuse et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with peripheral vascular graft/endograft infection, *in situ* reconstruction with autologous vein is recommended if removal of the infected graft is likely to lead to limb ischaemia.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Thermann and Wollert, Andersson et al., Monsen et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with peripheral vascular graft/endograft infection limited to only a part of the graft and in patients unfit for surgery, local irrigation and/or negative pressure wound therapy may be considered.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Verma et al., Armstrong et al., Cheng et al., Andersson et al., Monsen et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a peripheral vascular graft/endograft infection and a large tissue defect, negative pressure wound therapy should be considered in order to promote wound healing following infected graft removal and debridement with or without vascular reconstruction.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: Lejay et al., Ehsan and Gibbons, Zetrenne et al., Gabriel et al., Verhelst et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with peripheral vascular graft/endograft infection, <i>in situ reconstruction with cryopreserved allografts should be considered as an alternative after infected graft removal if it is likely to lead to limb ischaemia.

guideline_name: Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
evidence_first_authors: McMillan et al., Brewer et al., Mirzabeigi et al., Dua et al.
rec_text_verbatim: For patients with a peripheral vascular graft/endograft infection and a large tissue defect, muscle or musculocutaneous flaps should be considered to promote groin healing following graft removal and debridement with or without vascular reconstruction.
